hypothesis: Changing the third selected skill can change two different parts of the final memory: previously present items and items created by the last span. Measure each part's contribution to reader F1 and verify strict single-skill selection labels separately.
population: Use every window and every question in the frozen temporal_update_writer cohort. Keep all original statuses and track early and later panels separately. Record physically available parent pairs at registration; analyses based on pre-existing endpoints are retrospective. No validation or test labels are used.
mechanism: For both measured actions, replay the original prefix and exact parsed last write, verifying ordered memory text, stable IDs, versions, reader indices, prompts, answers and F1. Use the existing retriever and native per-session embedding batches. Factor final memory into surviving pre-span IDs and newly created IDs. Form two crossed banks with factual rows and their actual vectors. Label every read with source branch, memory ID and version. Verify both uncrossed readers before scoring any crossed contrast. If neither writer applied any mutation to a pre-existing ID, crossed banks equal the factual ones; record that structural identity. If the two old partitions differ, measure all questions and both crossed readers, including unchanged factual answers. Keep per-question results, any interaction, and equal-order marginal contributions on the F1 scale. Relative to the same native probabilities, these diagnostic components sum to the change in policy-weighted F1. No selected policy gets access to crossed answers.
credit: For every strict reference recovery in the parent pair, reproduce both endpoint answers and do same-skill evidence-write and retrieval controls on the weaker branch, using the source turn identities from the archived physical trace. Same-skill recovery, execution faults, failed reproduction or unavailable local writing evidence give zero selection credit. If writing evidence is unavailable, still test a hidden retrieval candidate when one exists. Only survived probes yield signed training credit. Partial F1 changes and mediated effects never count as additional selection credit.
